# Park + notify

<!-- Generated by `go run docs/roadmap/gen.go docs` from tickets.json. Do not edit by hand. -->

**Phase:** [P4 · Agents everywhere](../README.md#phase-4--agents-everywhere) · **Lane:** Worker · **Label:** `feature:park-notify` · **Epic:** [#221](https://github.com/ethosagent/warden/issues/221) · **Tickets:** 8 (4S 4M)

When a per-user OAuth grant is missing, the worker can hold the HTTP/1.1 request for a short time while the CP notifies the user with the connect link. If the user consents in time, the worker re-checks identity and policy, swaps the fresh token in and forwards the original request exactly once; otherwise the agent gets the unchanged Phase 3 JIT answer. Park reuses the Phase 3 pending, status and token paths (W-P3-JIT-01, W-P3-JIT-04, W-P3-PUS-09) and adds no new worker-to-CP route. It is off by default, and requests that already hold a grant pay nothing extra.

## How we build it

- Scope: park applies only to the Phase 3 per-user connect path, i.e. the jitDeny stage (W-P3-JIT-02) entered when W-P3-PUS-04 sets s.authRequired with reason grant_missing, scope_insufficient or reconsent_required. user_token_unavailable and authorization_unavailable (503) are never parked. Delegation-grant denies (mcp_grant_scope, p4-grants) are never parked, because a grant-bound token's tools claim cannot change mid-request; agents keep using the W-P4-DGR-08 grant long-poll for those. Nothing for park exists in code today: internal/park, internal/connect, internal/oauthbroker and internal/notify are all new (from P3/P4 tickets).
- Config: new CP-local sub-block `perUserSecrets.park: {enabled: false, agents: [], maxWait: 20s (1s-60s), notify: true, maxConcurrent: 256, maxPerUser: 8, maxBodyBytes: 1MiB (<= maxBodySwapSize, 10 MB), maxBufferedBytes: 64MiB, declineCooldown: 10m}` on PerUserSecretsConfig in internal/config/peruser.go (W-P3-PUS-02). It ships value-free inside the existing signed-bundle section `perUserSecrets` (W-P3-PUS-08) and is omitted when disabled, so /policy and bundle bytes stay identical to Phase 3. The worker applies it live through a new atomic Proxy seam SetPark on each bundle apply (W-P3-PUS-09); a worker without park support keeps the immediate JIT 403.
- Worker to CP: no new route and no new request field. The worker keeps calling POST /control/connect/pending (W-P3-JIT-01) through CreatePending (W-P3-JIT-02); the request wire shape is unchanged, so an older CP still answers. The CP reads park config for the verified act.sub from its own policy and returns an additive response object `notify: {queued: bool, kind, reason}`. A worker that sees no notify field treats it as queued=false and does not park. Because the CP only promises a park when the calling worker advertises `park/v1`, an older worker serving a park agent gets a plain connect_link message, never a 'your request is waiting' message for a request it already refused. sub, agent and scopes always come from the re-verified Warden token and the mapping, never from the worker.
- Notification (CP): exactly one user message per pending, guarded by the pending_authorizations.notified_at compare-and-set that W-P4-NTFY-05 adds; park plugs a KindSelector into that one send path instead of adding a second one. Kind is park_pending when the pending's agent is in park.agents, park.notify and notifications.kinds.park_pending are true, and the requesting worker's heartbeat caps include `park/v1`; otherwise connect_link (W-P4-NTFY-05); ref = pending:<pending_id> for both. Text uses only pending-row columns: agent id, provider display name, scopes, authorize_url and maxWait seconds; never host, path, method or any agent text. The CP returns queued=false with a reason when notify is off, no recipient or channel resolves, the notify rate limit hits, or a denied pending for the same (user_key, agent, provider) is younger than declineCooldown.
- Parkable request (worker): the agent is in park.agents; the CP said notify.queued=true with kind park_pending; the request is terminated HTTP/1.1 (not h2/gRPC, which keep the W-P3-JIT-06 answer, not an Upgrade/WebSocket, not Expect: 100-continue); X-Warden-Max-Wait is not 0; and the body is empty or has a known Content-Length <= park.maxBodyBytes, read with s.ensureBody() before parking. Admission takes a global slot (maxConcurrent), a per-user slot keyed by secrets.UserKey(idp_iss, sub) (maxPerUser) and buffered bytes (maxBufferedBytes). Anything else writes the JIT answer at once with outcome not_parkable, not_notifiable or overflow.
- Deadline: min(park.maxWait, X-Warden-Max-Wait integer seconds, 60s, pending expires_in) on the monotonic clock from jitDeny entry. The hint can only shorten the wait; 0 disables park for that request; invalid values are ignored. The header is stripped before forwarding with the same helper that strips X-Warden-Identity. The outcome is reported in a new X-Warden-Park-Outcome response header, so the Phase 3 403 body and its golden fixture stay unchanged.
- Waiter (new internal/park): Limiter (admission) and Waiter. Waiter keeps one in-flight CP long-poll per pending_id per worker and fans the result out to every local waiter; the poll is cancelled when the last waiter leaves, so the W-P3-JIT-04 limits (8 waiters per pending, 2,048 total) are not hit by one worker. It calls GET <CP endpoint>/connect/{pending_id}/status?wait=N with the worker credential on the W-P2-WCA-03 cert client through a new RemoteProvider.ConnectStatus; it never follows status_url (on consent.publicURL) and never uses the status_token. N = ceil(remaining) clamped to 1-60s; 429, 5xx and transport errors back off with jitter (honouring Retry-After) until the deadline. Outcomes use connect.Status: granted, denied, expired, plus timeout, client_gone, shutdown and cp_unavailable.
- Client-gone safety: with the body fully read, one goroutine runs s.br.Peek(1) on the session reader. EOF or an error cancels the park (client_gone) and nothing is forwarded; a pipelined byte stays buffered. To stop it, tlsConn.SetReadDeadline(time.Now()) unblocks the peek, the goroutine is joined, and the deadline is reset to zero before any other read. The proxy sets no read deadlines today, so this is new code in internal/proxy. Park contexts derive from the ctx passed to Proxy.Serve (internal/proxy/serve.go), so worker shutdown cancels every park (outcome shutdown) and writes the JIT 403 with Connection: close.
- Resume on granted: drop the W-P3-JIT-02 pending-cache entry for (user_key, agent, provider); re-check the host against the live allowlist snapshot, agent_disabled and connIdentity expiry; restore the pre-swap headers, RawQuery and buffered body kept by W-P3-PUS-04/05, reset s.refs and s.swappedNames, and re-run swapSecrets (static swap plus the per-user resolver, which mints through UserTokenSource.AccessToken; the CP mint re-checks exp, session revocation and block list). Then the normal applyTransforms, forward and relayResponse stages run, so the request is forwarded exactly once. UserTokenSource.Invalidate is not called, because grant errors are never cached. Any failure writes that path's normal response (policy deny, identity_required, user_token_unavailable 503, or a fresh authorization_required) and never parks a second time.
- MCP: on the forward-proxy path a tools/call parks silently under the same rules and, if not resumed, gets the W-P3-JIT-03 result or -32042 error unchanged; the proxy path never writes progress, because that would commit a 200 text/event-stream before the upstream answers. Progress notifications are sent only from the MCP gateway hub (internal/mcp/hub, W-P4-MGW-03/07), which owns the session response: when params._meta.progressToken is present and the client accepts text/event-stream, it sends notifications/progress with the CP message and authorize_url, and notifications/cancelled for the parked id cancels the park. The hub path parks when notify.queued=true or a progressToken is present.
- Degraded modes: CP down at park start gives the JIT-02 503 authorization_unavailable with no park; CP down mid-wait gives bounded backoff and then the JIT 403 at the deadline (outcome cp_unavailable). IdP down means the user cannot sign in and the park times out. A worker restart drops parked connections while the pending persists on the CP; a CP restart drops long-polls and the waiter re-polls. On multi-replica CPs a wake can lag up to the JIT-04 5s re-read. Park guarantees at most one forward per request, not per logical operation: a client that retries on a new connection while the first is still parked can produce two forwards, so the default maxWait (20s) stays below common client timeouts and docs tell agent authors to set client timeouts above maxWait + 5s.
- Observability: worker OTel instruments warden.park.total{outcome,provider}, warden.park.wait (histogram, seconds) and warden.park.active (up-down counter); CP counter warden_cp_park_notify_total{outcome}, following the CP naming of warden_cp_connect_pending_total. provider is a configured id or `other`; no sub or agent labels. The wait is excluded from warden.request.added_latency. Events keep Reason authorization_required on non-resumed parks and add Event.ParkOutcome and Event.ParkWaitMs (omitempty, additive SQLite and fleet columns); a resumed request records ParkOutcome=resumed on its single forwarding event. No body, token, status_token or query string appears in any log, event or notification.

## Done when

In the in-process integration setup of W-P3-PUS-11/W-P3-JIT-07 (CP with consent, broker and portal, an enrolled worker, perUserSecrets with a fake OAuth provider, a fake Slack integration) with `perUserSecrets.park` enabled for one agent: a user with no grant sends a 200 KiB POST to a mapped domain, gets exactly one notification with the authorize link, and the fake upstream sees zero requests until consent; completing consent within maxWait delivers the original request upstream exactly once with the user's token and returns the upstream response to the agent. Timeout and decline return the unchanged Phase 3 authorization_required 403 with X-Warden-Park-Outcome set; a client that disconnects mid-park causes no upstream request; overflow, an over-cap or chunked body, an h2/gRPC call and an unnotifiable user get the immediate JIT answer. A gateway tools/call with a progressToken receives a progress notification with the authorize URL and then the result. No body, token or status_token appears in any log, event or notification, and with park disabled the bundle and worker behaviour are byte-identical to Phase 3.

### 1/8 · W-P4-PARK-01

**Add perUserSecrets.park config and ship it in the signed bundle**

Type **feature** · Size **S** · Issue [#222](https://github.com/ethosagent/warden/issues/222)

Add the park settings as a sub-block of the CP-local perUserSecrets config, because park only applies to per-user mappings. Ship them value-free inside the existing signed-bundle section `perUserSecrets` and apply them on the worker through a new atomic Proxy seam. Nothing reads the seam until W-P4-PARK-04, and with the block absent the bundle stays byte-identical.

**Requirements**

- New `PerUserSecretsConfig.Park *ParkConfig` in internal/config/peruser.go (W-P3-PUS-02) parsed from `perUserSecrets.park` with KnownFields strict: enabled (false), agents ([]), maxWait (20s), notify (true), maxConcurrent (256), maxPerUser (8), maxBodyBytes (1 MiB), maxBufferedBytes (64 MiB), declineCooldown (10m).
- Validation: maxWait 1s-60s (60s is the constant park.MaxWaitCap, equal to the W-P3-JIT-04 status wait clamp); maxConcurrent 1-4096; maxPerUser 1..maxConcurrent; maxBodyBytes 0..maxBodySwapSize and <= maxBufferedBytes; declineCooldown 0-24h; each agents entry must appear in at least one perUserSecrets mapping's agents list. Errors name the field.
- The W-P3-PUS-08 section type gains an omitempty `park` object carrying the same fields with durations as integer seconds (maxWaitSeconds, declineCooldownSeconds). It holds no value-bearing field, so the existing reflect test still passes. A disabled or absent block is omitted, and the section bytes stay identical.
- The CP logs a warning at load (no failure) when park.enabled is true but consent.providers or notifications are not configured, because park can then never trigger.
- Worker: the bundle apply path of W-P3-PUS-09 builds a proxy.ParkConfig and calls a new Proxy.SetPark (atomic.Pointer, same pattern as SetJudge and SetDLP in internal/proxy/proxy.go); nil means disabled. In-flight parks keep their deadline; new limits apply to new parks only.
- One info log on apply with enabled, agent count, maxWaitSeconds, maxConcurrent and maxPerUser; nothing else.
- RemoteProvider.Heartbeat adds cap `park/v1` (the binary can park); the W-P3-PUS-09 section decoder ignores the unknown omitempty `park` object on older workers, and the CP never sends park_pending to a worker without the cap (W-P4-PARK-02).

**Implementation plan**

1. internal/config/peruser.go: add new type ParkConfig, defaults and validation; wire it into PerUserSecretsConfig parsing and EncodeNode.
2. Bundle section builder from W-P3-PUS-08 (CP side): add the omitempty park object built from ParkConfig; extend the section reflect test and the byte-identical golden test.
3. internal/proxy/proxy.go: add new ParkConfig struct, parkP atomic.Pointer, SetPark and parkConfig() accessors.
4. internal/worker/usertoken.go (W-P3-PUS-09) bundle apply: map the section's park object to proxy.ParkConfig and call SetPark; a section without park calls SetPark(nil).
5. Tests: internal/config TestParkValidation and TestParkDefaults; section TestParkSectionOmittedWhenDisabled; internal/worker TestApplyParkHotReload (set then clear without restart).

**Acceptance criteria**

- [ ] Given `perUserSecrets.park.maxWait: 61s` or `maxPerUser: 0`, config load fails with an error naming the field: `go test ./internal/config -run TestParkValidation`.
- [ ] Given park absent or enabled=false, the signed perUserSecrets section bytes equal the pre-change golden copy.
- [ ] Given park enabled, the section round-trips with maxWaitSeconds 20 and no value-bearing field (reflect test passes).
- [ ] Applying a bundle with park and then one without sets and then clears the proxy seam with no restart: `go test ./internal/worker -run TestApplyParkHotReload`.
- [ ] `go test ./internal/config ./internal/worker ./internal/controlplane` passes.

**Depends on:** [`W-P3-PUS-02`](refresh-model.md#212--w-p3-pus-02) Add the CP-local perUserSecrets config block and the Vault consent.store backend; [`W-P3-PUS-08`](refresh-model.md#812--w-p3-pus-08) Serve perUserSecrets and userGrantEpochs as signed-bundle sections; [`W-P3-PUS-09`](refresh-model.md#912--w-p3-pus-09) Add the worker UserTokenSource with memory cache and epoch invalidation

### 2/8 · W-P4-PARK-02

**Notify the user once per pending when the agent can park**

Type **feature** · Size **M** · Issue [#223](https://github.com/ethosagent/warden/issues/223)

Extend the W-P3-JIT-01 create-or-reuse logic so the CP itself decides whether to notify the user, using its own park config for the verified agent. No new route and no new request field are added, so older workers and older CPs interoperate; the response gains an additive notify object that tells the worker whether a park is worthwhile. Exactly one message is sent per pending, and a recent decline suppresses new messages.

**Requirements**

- No new route. After JIT-01 verifies subject_token and takes act.sub, the CP looks up perUserSecrets.park for that agent. The JIT-01 request shape, 32 KiB cap and DisallowUnknownFields stay unchanged.
- Reuse the notified_at, notify_kind and notify_status columns and the GrantStore.MarkNotified compare-and-set from W-P4-NTFY-05 (no new migration): park installs a KindSelector on that single send path, so racing workers, reuse of the pending and connect_link never send twice for one pending_id. On reuse of a pending that was never notified (for example, notifications enabled after it was created), the same claim runs.
- Kind is park_pending when park.enabled, the agent is in park.agents, park.notify and notifications.kinds.park_pending are true, and the calling worker principal's heartbeat caps (W-P1-BLOCK-04) include `park/v1`; otherwise connect_link as W-P4-NTFY-05 defines (when notifications.kinds.connect_link is true). ref = pending:<pending_id> for both kinds.
- Content comes only from pending-row columns: agent id, provider display name, scopes, authorize_url and maxWait seconds. Never host, path, method or agent-supplied text. The recipient is resolved from the row's user_key, never from worker input.
- Decline cooldown: when a denied pending for the same (user_key, agent_id, provider) completed less than declineCooldown ago, nothing is sent and the response says queued=false, reason declined_recently.
- Response gains additive `notify: {queued: bool, kind, reason}` with reason in sent|already_sent|disabled|no_channel|rate_limited|declined_recently|failed. The send runs asynchronously through notify.Service.Send (W-P4-NTFY-04): queued=true means the send was accepted, and a delivery failure is recorded on the row and never fails the pending call.
- Counter warden_cp_park_notify_total{outcome} following warden_cp_connect_pending_total. One info log with pending_id, agent, provider and outcome; no sub, email or status_token. The send is a machine event: it is recorded in the notify_outbox row and the `warden.notify.v1` line (W-P4-NTFY-04), not in the admin audit chain.

**Implementation plan**

1. internal/oauthbroker (W-P3-JIT-01 handler): after create-or-reuse, call a new notifyPending(ctx, row, agentPark) helper in a new file park_notify.go.
2. Add GrantStore.LastDenied(ctx, userKey, agent, provider) for the cooldown; reuse GrantStore.MarkNotified and the KindSelector seam from W-P4-NTFY-05 instead of a new migration.
3. parkKindSelector: pick the kind (including the `park/v1` cap check), check decline cooldown; the W-P4-NTFY-05 path then claims notified_at and calls notify.Service.Send in a goroutine bounded by a 10s context and record notify_status on completion.
4. internal/connect: add the omitempty Notify field to the pending response struct; the worker CreatePending decoder (W-P3-JIT-02) ignores unknown fields and treats a missing Notify as queued=false.
5. Register warden_cp_park_notify_total next to warden_cp_connect_pending_total.
6. Tests in internal/oauthbroker park_notify_test.go: concurrency, kind choice, cooldown, content and failure cases with a fake notifier.

**Acceptance criteria**

- [ ] Given 20 concurrent pending calls for the same user, agent and provider with park enabled, exactly one park_pending send happens and one row has notified_at set: `go test -race ./internal/oauthbroker -run TestParkNotifyOncePerPending`.
- [ ] Given park disabled and notifications.kinds.connect_link true, the pending gets one connect_link send and no park_pending; given both off, nothing is sent and notify.queued is false with reason disabled.
- [ ] Given a denied pending for the same key 5 minutes ago and declineCooldown 10m, no send happens and the response has queued=false, reason declined_recently.
- [ ] Given a fake notifier that fails, the pending call still returns 201 with the same body plus notify.queued=true, and the row records notify_status failed.
- [ ] The captured message contains authorize_url and the provider display name but not the request host or path: `go test ./internal/oauthbroker -run TestParkNotifyContent`.
- [ ] `go test ./internal/controlplane -run TestAuthzRouteCoverage` passes with no new route.
- [ ] Given park enabled for the agent but a calling worker whose heartbeat lacks `park/v1`, the pending gets one connect_link send, no park_pending, and the response notify is {queued: true, kind: connect_link}: `go test ./internal/oauthbroker -run TestParkNotifyNeedsCap`.

### 3/8 · W-P4-PARK-03

**Add the park limiter and coalescing status waiter**

Type **feature** · Size **M** · Issue [#224](https://github.com/ethosagent/warden/issues/224)

Create internal/park with the admission limiter and the waiter that long-polls the CP status endpoint with the worker credential. One status poll per pending_id is shared by all local waiters, so a worker never hits the CP waiter limits from W-P3-JIT-04. This is a worker-only library with no wiring, so merging it changes no behaviour.

**Requirements**

- New package internal/park (imports internal/connect, never internal/proxy). `Limiter.Acquire(userKey string, bodyBytes int64) (release func(), ok bool)` enforces maxConcurrent, maxPerUser keyed by secrets.UserKey(idp_iss, sub) and maxBufferedBytes, with no I/O and no goroutines.
- `Waiter.Wait(ctx, pendingID string, deadline time.Time) Outcome` with Outcome granted|denied|expired|timeout|client_gone|shutdown|cp_unavailable, mapped from connect.Status. Context cancellation returns within 100ms; the caller says whether the cancel cause was client_gone or shutdown.
- Status client: new RemoteProvider.ConnectStatus(ctx, pendingID, wait) on the W-P2-WCA-03 shared cert client calls GET <CP endpoint>/connect/{url.PathEscape(id)}/status?wait=N. It never follows status_url, never sends the status_token, uses an HTTP timeout of wait+5s and caps the response at 4 KiB.
- N = ceil(remaining) clamped to 1-60s. 429, 5xx and transport errors retry with jittered backoff (250ms doubling, max 2s, Retry-After honoured) until the deadline, then return cp_unavailable. 404 (old CP or credential mismatch) returns cp_unavailable at once.
- Coalescing: at most one in-flight status poll per pending_id per worker, fanned out to every local waiter, cancelled when the last waiter leaves. No lock is held across network I/O.
- Deadlines use the monotonic clock. Logs carry pending_id and outcome only; never the status_token or sub.
- The status call is a worker-to-CP call, so it carries only the worker cert principal (W-P2-WCA-04 mTLS; a wwt_ bearer is not used), stays inside the W-P3-JIT-04 per-pending and total waiter limits plus the coalescing above, and the CP re-checks that the pending's agent_id equals the principal's heartbeat agentID.

**Implementation plan**

1. New internal/park/limiter.go: Limiter with a global counter, per-user map and byte budget under one mutex.
2. New internal/park/waiter.go: Waiter with a map[pendingID]*poll; each poll runs one goroutine that loops ConnectStatus and broadcasts the terminal result through a closed channel.
3. New StatusClient interface in internal/park; implement it in internal/worker (RemoteProvider.ConnectStatus, new) over the W-P2-WCA-03 client, building the URL from the configured CP endpoint.
4. New helpers park.EffectiveDeadline(start, maxWait, hint, expiresIn) and park.ParseHint(header) (integer seconds 0-60, invalid ignored, 0 = opt out).
5. Tests with an httptest fake status server and a fake clock: granted, coalescing, limiter, cancel, backoff and URL cases, all under -race.

**Acceptance criteria**

- [ ] Given a fake server that returns pending and then granted after 300ms, Wait returns granted within 400ms: `go test -race ./internal/park -run TestWaitGranted`.
- [ ] Given 20 waiters on one pending_id, the fake server sees at most one concurrent request and all 20 get the same outcome: `go test -race ./internal/park -run TestWaitCoalesces`.
- [ ] Given maxPerUser 2, a third Acquire for the same user key returns ok=false while another key succeeds; given maxBufferedBytes 1 MiB, a 2 MiB Acquire returns ok=false: `go test ./internal/park -run TestLimiter`.
- [ ] Given ctx cancelled mid-poll, Wait returns within 100ms and the in-flight request to the fake is cancelled.
- [ ] Given a fake that always returns 503, Wait returns cp_unavailable at the deadline (fake clock); given 404, it returns at once.
- [ ] The request path is /connect/<id>/status on the CP endpoint even when the pending's status_url points at another host, and no Authorization Bearer status_token is sent.

### 4/8 · W-P4-PARK-04

**Park and resume HTTP/1.1 requests in the jitDeny stage**

Type **feature** · Size **M** · Issue [#225](https://github.com/ethosagent/warden/issues/225)

Add the park branch to the jitDeny stage so an eligible HTTP/1.1 request waits for consent instead of getting the 403 at once. On granted the worker re-checks policy and identity, restores the pre-swap request, re-runs the swap and forwards exactly once; on any other outcome it writes the unchanged Phase 3 answer. MCP tools/call on the proxy path parks silently and keeps the W-P3-JIT-03 result shapes.

**Requirements**

- Park only after CreatePending returns status pending with notify.queued=true and notify.kind=park_pending, and only when: the park seam is non-nil; the bound agent is in park.agents; the request is terminated HTTP/1.1 (not h2/gRPC, not an Upgrade, not Expect: 100-continue); X-Warden-Max-Wait is not 0; the body is empty or has a known Content-Length <= maxBodyBytes and s.ensureBody() succeeds; and Limiter.Acquire succeeds. Otherwise the existing JIT answer is written at once.
- Deadline = park.EffectiveDeadline(jitDeny entry, maxWait, X-Warden-Max-Wait, pending expires_in). X-Warden-Max-Wait is removed from the request whenever park is enabled, using the X-Warden-Identity strip helper.
- Client-gone watcher: a goroutine runs s.br.Peek(1); EOF or an error cancels the wait (client_gone), data does not. It is stopped with s.tlsConn.SetReadDeadline(time.Now()), joined, and the deadline reset to zero before any further read. On client_gone nothing is forwarded and the session ends without a response.
- The park context derives from the ctx passed to Proxy.Serve (internal/proxy/serve.go); on shutdown the worker writes the JIT 403 with Connection: close.
- Resume on granted: drop the JIT pending-cache entry; re-check the live allowlist verdict for s.domain, agent_disabled and connIdentity expiry; restore the W-P3-PUS-04/05 pre-swap headers, RawQuery and body; reset s.refs and s.swappedNames; re-run swapSecrets and continue to applyTransforms, forward and relayResponse. A grant error on the re-mint writes the JIT 403 without a second park; user_token_unavailable writes the PUS-04 503. UserTokenSource.Invalidate is not called.
- timeout, denied, expired, overflow and cp_unavailable write the Phase 3 JIT 403 or W-P3-JIT-03 JSON-RPC answer unchanged, plus X-Warden-Park-Outcome. The proxy path never writes MCP progress.
- Hot path: with the seam nil or a grant present, no extra allocations, locks or goroutines. Exactly one event per request; no body, token or status_token is logged.

**Implementation plan**

1. New internal/proxy/park.go: p.tryPark(s, pending) (eligibility, Limiter, Waiter) called from jitDeny in internal/proxy/jit.go (W-P3-JIT-02) before the 403 is written.
2. New watchClientGone(s) in park.go with the Peek/SetReadDeadline/join/reset sequence; first use of read deadlines in internal/proxy.
3. Resume helper p.resumeParked(s): policy and identity re-check, snapshot restore (reuse the W-P3-PUS-05 restore function), swapSecrets re-run; jitDeny then returns endSession=false so runRequestStages continues to applyTransforms.
4. Wire the park ctx from Proxy.Serve into a new Proxy field set at Serve start.
5. Add X-Warden-Park-Outcome to the JIT response writer (writeJSONResponse from W-P3-JIT-02) when a park ran.
6. Tests in internal/proxy/park_test.go with a fake CP (pending, status) and fake upstream, all under -race, plus a pipelined-request test.

**Acceptance criteria**

- [ ] Given park enabled, maxWait 5s and a fake CP that grants after 500ms, the agent gets the upstream 200 and the fake upstream records exactly one request with the fake provider token: `go test -race ./internal/proxy -run TestParkResume`.
- [ ] Given the client closes the TLS conn 200ms into the park, the upstream records zero requests and the goroutine count returns to baseline: `go test -race ./internal/proxy -run TestParkClientGone`.
- [ ] Given no grant within the wait, or X-Warden-Max-Wait: 1, the body equals internal/proxy/testdata/jit/authorization_required.golden.json and X-Warden-Park-Outcome is timeout: `go test ./internal/proxy -run TestParkTimeoutGolden`.
- [ ] Given a body over maxBodyBytes, a chunked body, an h2 stream, a full Limiter or notify.queued=false, the JIT answer is returned with zero status polls.
- [ ] Given the host removed from the allowlist while parked, the resumed request is denied and the upstream sees zero requests; the forwarded request never carries X-Warden-Max-Wait; a pipelined second request on the same connection is served after a resume.
- [ ] Given a proxied MCP tools/call that times out, the response equals the W-P3-JIT-03 tools/call result and contains no notifications/progress: `go test ./internal/proxy -run TestParkMCPTimeout`.
- [ ] With park disabled, `go test ./internal/proxy` passes unchanged and `go test ./internal/proxy -run x -bench BenchmarkHandleHTTPKeepAlive -benchmem` shows no added allocs/op.

**Depends on:** [`W-P4-PARK-02`](park-notify.md#28--w-p4-park-02) Notify the user once per pending when the agent can park; [`W-P4-PARK-03`](park-notify.md#38--w-p4-park-03) Add the park limiter and coalescing status waiter; [`W-P3-JIT-03`](jit-authorization.md#37--w-p3-jit-03) Return JSON-RPC results for MCP calls missing a grant; [`W-P3-PUS-05`](refresh-model.md#512--w-p3-pus-05) Retry once on upstream 401 with a CP-refreshed token

**Unblocks:** [`W-P4-PARK-06`](park-notify.md#68--w-p4-park-06) Record park outcomes on events and metrics; [`W-P4-PARK-07`](park-notify.md#78--w-p4-park-07) Add the park end-to-end integration test; [`W-P4-PARK-08`](park-notify.md#88--w-p4-park-08) Document park for operators and agent authors

### 5/8 · W-P4-PARK-05

**Park MCP gateway tool calls with progress notifications**

Type **feature** · Size **M** · Issue [#226](https://github.com/ethosagent/warden/issues/226)

Add parking to the MCP gateway hub, where the gateway owns the Streamable HTTP response and can send progress notifications safely. When a per-user upstream connection is missing (W-P4-MGW-07), the hub creates the pending, waits through internal/park and, if the client sent a progressToken, shows the authorize link through notifications/progress. The forward-proxy path is covered by W-P4-PARK-04 and never sends progress.

**Requirements**

- In the W-P4-MGW-07 per-user path of internal/mcp/hub, when resolution reports a grant error and park is enabled for the agent, the hub calls CreatePending, then Limiter.Acquire and Waiter.Wait. It parks when notify.queued=true or the call carries params._meta.progressToken.
- With a progressToken and an Accept header that allows text/event-stream, the hub answers as SSE and sends notifications/progress {progressToken, progress (strictly increasing elapsed seconds), message} at once and every 10s, with a 15s SSE comment heartbeat. message is the CP message plus authorize_url, capped at 1 KiB.
- Without a progressToken the hub waits silently and replies with the normal JSON or SSE result.
- On granted the hub re-resolves the credential through the W-P3-PUS-09 UserTokenSource, opens or reuses the per-user upstream session keyed (idp_iss, sub, registryId) as W-P4-MGW-07 defines and forwards the call once; OnResponse checks still run. On timeout, denied, expired or overflow it returns the W-P3-JIT-03 MCPToolResult with the id echoed.
- notifications/cancelled whose requestId matches the parked call, a gateway session DELETE, an idle-out or a client disconnect cancels the park (client_gone); the tool is never called upstream.
- Progress text never contains a token, status_token, sub or upstream output. Calls that already hold a connection do no park work; internal/mcp/stdio is not changed.

**Implementation plan**

1. internal/mcp/hub (W-P4-MGW-03/07): add a new parkToolCall helper in a new file park.go that takes the pending, the park.Limiter and the park.Waiter.
2. Add a cancel registry keyed by JSON-RPC id per session so notifications/cancelled can cancel a parked call.
3. Emit progress events with the existing internal/mcp/sse writer helpers; build the final result with the W-P3-JIT-03 builders in internal/connect.
4. Share the worker's park.Limiter and park.Waiter instances with the hub at wiring time in internal/worker.
5. Tests in internal/mcp/hub park_test.go with a fake CP, fake upstream and SSE client.

**Acceptance criteria**

- [ ] Given a hub tools/call with progressToken 'p1' and a grant after 1s, the client sees at least one notifications/progress with progressToken 'p1' and the authorize_url, then the upstream result with the original id: `go test -race ./internal/mcp/hub -run TestParkProgress`.
- [ ] Given the same call without _meta.progressToken, no notifications/progress is emitted and the result still arrives after the grant.
- [ ] Given notifications/cancelled for the parked id, the fake upstream records zero tools/call: `go test ./internal/mcp/hub -run TestParkCancelled`.
- [ ] Given no grant within maxWait, the result fields equal the W-P3-JIT-03 builder output: `go test ./internal/mcp/hub -run TestParkTimeoutToolError`.
- [ ] `git diff --stat main -- internal/mcp/stdio` is empty.

**Depends on:** [`W-P4-PARK-02`](park-notify.md#28--w-p4-park-02) Notify the user once per pending when the agent can park; [`W-P4-PARK-03`](park-notify.md#38--w-p4-park-03) Add the park limiter and coalescing status waiter; [`W-P4-MGW-07`](mcp-gateway.md#715--w-p4-mgw-07) Use per-user credentials for gateway upstreams; [`W-P3-JIT-03`](jit-authorization.md#37--w-p3-jit-03) Return JSON-RPC results for MCP calls missing a grant

### 6/8 · W-P4-PARK-06

**Record park outcomes on events and metrics**

Type **feature** · Size **S** · Issue [#227](https://github.com/ethosagent/warden/issues/227)

Add OTel instruments and additive event fields for park outcomes, so operators can see how often parks resume and how long users take. The Phase 3 deny reason authorization_required stays unchanged, so alert and dashboard consumers are not affected. Events without park stay byte-identical.

**Requirements**

- internal/observability: counter warden.park.total{outcome,provider} with outcome in resumed|timeout|denied|expired|client_gone|shutdown|overflow|not_parkable|not_notifiable|cp_unavailable, histogram warden.park.wait (seconds, buckets up to 60) and up-down counter warden.park.active. provider is a configured id or `other`; no sub or agent labels. Nil-safe like the existing instruments.
- analytics.Event gains ParkOutcome (json park_outcome) and ParkWaitMs (json park_wait_ms), both omitempty, added with addColumnIfAbsent to the local SQLite store and FleetSQLiteStore and carried on AggregatedEvent (W-P3-PUS-10 pattern).
- Non-resumed parks keep Reason authorization_required; no new value is added to internal/proxy/reasons.go, so bridgeEvent in internal/alertpipeline still raises no finding.
- The park wait is excluded from warden.request.added_latency and from the resumed event's latency; ParkWaitMs carries it instead.
- The decision log line gains park_outcome when set.
- No body, token, status_token or query string is recorded.

**Implementation plan**

1. internal/observability/observability.go: register the three instruments in newMetrics and add new methods RecordPark(outcome, provider), ObserveParkWait(d) and AddParkActive(delta).
2. internal/analytics: add the two fields, columns and migrations in both stores and AggregatedEvent.
3. internal/proxy/park.go (W-P4-PARK-04): set the fields on the single event, call the metric methods, and subtract the wait from s.reqStart-based latency.
4. Tests: observability TestParkMetrics, analytics TestParkColumnsRoundTrip plus migration of an old DB, proxy TestParkEventNoSecrets.

**Acceptance criteria**

- [ ] After one resumed and one timed-out park, warden.park.total shows resumed=1 and timeout=1 and warden.park.wait has 2 observations: `go test ./internal/observability -run TestParkMetrics`.
- [ ] A stored resumed event has decision allow, park_outcome resumed and park_wait_ms > 0; a timeout event has Reason authorization_required and park_outcome timeout; an event without park has neither JSON key.
- [ ] An old SQLite database migrates and round-trips both columns: `go test ./internal/analytics -run TestParkColumnsRoundTrip`.
- [ ] A sentinel string in the request body and the provider token is absent from all captured logs and stored events: `go test ./internal/proxy -run TestParkEventNoSecrets`.

**Depends on:** [`W-P4-PARK-04`](park-notify.md#48--w-p4-park-04) Park and resume HTTP/1.1 requests in the jitDeny stage; [`W-P3-PUS-10`](refresh-model.md#1012--w-p3-pus-10) Record the per-user token provider on analytics events

**Unblocks:** [`W-P4-PARK-07`](park-notify.md#78--w-p4-park-07) Add the park end-to-end integration test

### 7/8 · W-P4-PARK-07

**Add the park end-to-end integration test**

Type **test** · Size **S** · Issue [#330](https://github.com/ethosagent/warden/issues/330)

Prove the feature's done_when in one integration test with in-process fakes, so CI needs no Docker. It reuses the W-P3-JIT-07 setup and adds a fake Slack integration and park config. It changes no production code.

**Requirements**

- Build tag integration in test/integration; in-process CP with consent, broker, portal and notifications with a fake Slack integration; a worker enrolled with a W-P2-WCA test cert; perUserSecrets with park enabled for one agent; a fake OAuth provider and a counting fake upstream.
- Cases: resumed (consent through /portal/connect/{id}, /connect/start and /connect/callback within maxWait), timeout, decline then cooldown, client disconnect, and CP stopped mid-park.
- Asserts exactly one notification per pending and exactly one upstream request on resume, zero otherwise.
- Captures every log line, stored event and notification payload and asserts none contains a sentinel body string, access token, status_token or subject token.
- Runs in under 60s.

**Implementation plan**

1. Extend the W-P3-JIT-07 test harness in test/integration with park config and a fake Slack HTTP server.
2. Add new test/integration/park_test.go with one subtest per case.
3. Add log, event and notification capture with the sentinel scan.

**Acceptance criteria**

- [ ] `go test -tags integration ./test/integration -run TestParkResume` passes: the original request reaches the upstream exactly once after consent.
- [ ] `go test -tags integration ./test/integration -run TestParkTimeout` passes: the agent gets the JIT 403 at maxWait (within 1s) and the upstream sees zero requests.
- [ ] The client-disconnect and CP-down subtests see zero upstream requests.
- [ ] The sentinel scan finds no body, token or status_token in any captured output.
- [ ] `scripts/check.sh --integration` passes.

**Depends on:** [`W-P4-PARK-04`](park-notify.md#48--w-p4-park-04) Park and resume HTTP/1.1 requests in the jitDeny stage; [`W-P4-PARK-06`](park-notify.md#68--w-p4-park-06) Record park outcomes on events and metrics; [`W-P3-JIT-07`](jit-authorization.md#77--w-p3-jit-07) Add end-to-end test for the JIT consent loop; [`W-P4-NTFY-02`](user-notify.md#210--w-p4-ntfy-02) Add Slack integration with DM delivery by email lookup

### 8/8 · W-P4-PARK-08

**Document park for operators and agent authors**

Type **docs** · Size **S** · Issue [#331](https://github.com/ethosagent/warden/issues/331)

Extend the Phase 3 JIT documentation so operators know what park holds on a worker and agent authors know how to set client timeouts and the wait hint. The timeout answer is the Phase 3 contract unchanged, which the docs state plainly. A drift test keeps the documented config keys equal to the code.

**Requirements**

- docs/jit-authorization.md (W-P3-JIT-05) gains a Park section: what is parked (HTTP/1.1 and MCP over HTTP; h2 and gRPC are not), the body cap, X-Warden-Max-Wait semantics (integer seconds, shorten only, 0 opts out), X-Warden-Park-Outcome values, and that the timeout answer is unchanged.
- Agent guidance: set client read timeouts above maxWait + 5s; park guarantees at most one forward per request, not per logical operation; retry non-idempotent calls only after the user confirms.
- Operator guidance: perUserSecrets.park keys and defaults, memory bound (maxBufferedBytes), that parked requests hold worker connections, decline cooldown, and CP-first upgrade order.
- docs/architecture.md and docs/control-plane.md describe the park-only worker GET /connect/{id}/status call and the additive notify field on the pending response.
- A doc test fails when a perUserSecrets.park key in internal/config is missing from the docs.

**Implementation plan**

1. Write the Park section and outcome table in docs/jit-authorization.md.
2. Update docs/architecture.md and docs/control-plane.md worker-to-CP call lists.
3. Add a key-drift test next to the existing JIT-05 doc drift test.

**Acceptance criteria**

- [ ] docs/jit-authorization.md lists every perUserSecrets.park key with its default and bound.
- [ ] docs/architecture.md and docs/control-plane.md mention the worker status call used by park.
- [ ] `go test ./docs/... ./internal/config -run TestParkDocKeys` passes, and fails when a key is removed from the doc.

**Depends on:** [`W-P4-PARK-04`](park-notify.md#48--w-p4-park-04) Park and resume HTTP/1.1 requests in the jitDeny stage; [`W-P3-JIT-05`](jit-authorization.md#57--w-p3-jit-05) Document the authorization_required contract
